hypothesis: The rail ledger's per-operation cost does not scale with the number of holders, and it is far below the previous 128-slot ledger.

conditions.configurations: 42 clock and 16 rail leases, then 126 clock leases and a full rail table; previous ledger 127 rail leases when full, current ledger 31
conditions.compile_flags: -march=armv8-a -mstrict-align -O2, tuned for Cortex-A55, run once per operation under Unicorn

conclusion: Costs are independent of holder count and meet the design budgets.
narrative: Comparison table (16 leases / full table). Rail status, one-rail token: previous 222 / 888 instructions and 34 / 256 lines, current 37 / 37 instructions and 3 / 3 lines. Clock token status: previous 235 / 592, current 45 / 45. Acquire, poll and release: previous 1,643 / 3,565, current 335 / 335. Borrow: previous 823 / 1,531, current 153 / 153. End borrow: previous 271 / 923, current 86 / 86. Authority check per PMIC transaction: previous 498 / 1,507, current 6 / 6 instructions and 1 line. Ledger storage: previous 20,096 bytes, current 1,600 bytes. The previous ledger had 128 slots, so its full configuration held 127 rail leases; the current ledger holds 31. Equal costs in the two configurations show that no operation scans holders. The power-domain row read costs 12 instructions with one acquire load and no exclusive access, against one DE_SYS provider poll at the merge base of 344 instructions with a lock entry and two register reads. Load/store exclusive instructions and the ARMv8.1 LSE atomics (CAS, SWP, LDADD and the other atomic memory operations) count as exclusive accesses. checks/rail-leases-cost.py enforces the budgets of docs/designs/power-authority.md with --limits.

hypothesis: The rail ledger grants, polls and releases all fifteen outputs in production order and retains state on every fault.
conclusion: Metadata behavior only; physical PMIC, rail and peripheral qualification remains pending.
narrative: checks/rail-leases.c and its runner checks/rail-leases.py (removed: an evidence-preserving one-off batch covered by rail-leases-cost) built the ledger with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and covered acquire, poll and release in production order for all fifteen outputs with no registry or GPU lease and no bus access; refusal of every other output; exclusion; aliases; a full table; never-reused identifiers; borrow capacity; fault retention, including a registry fault reported in the state word; and row pins. The runner compiled every affected native unit with its recorded flags and archived inputs and the executable.
